Show or hide the Map Information window: the world map with the map tiles over it, and the Map Information Editor. It docks like the other Map Editor windows, e.g. beside the viewport.

The world map with the map tiles over it. {0} on the map picks the maps there, to load from Selected Tiles.

If enabled, the large tile shapes will overlay the map.

Each large map tile has a map information file (other/mapinfotex) holding four layers at 4 m per pixel. Each pixel is the ID of a row in the layer's param, which decides what the game uses at that spot.
Map information files are only used by Elden Ring.
This map source has no map information. Switch the Map Source to Lands Between or Shadow of the Erdtree.
The map information files of the shown map.

{0} tiles have an image the game wouldn't load, so a layer can't be edited there. Hover a tile to see which.
The layer to show and paint. Painting a layer leaves the other layers as they are.
Red channel of the first image: a row of {0}, giving the save map name and the multiplayer area.
Green channel of the first image: a row of {0}, giving the place name shown on screen (and in the DLC the BGM and environment place).
Blue channel of the first image: a row of {0}, giving the weather lot used by default.
Red channel of the second image (_01): a row of {0}, giving the mimicry establishment param.
What clicking on the map does.
Paint the selected value in a circle. Strokes cross tile edges.
Replace the connected area of the clicked value with the selected value, across tile edges.
Click to select the value under the cursor. {0} picks with any tool.
The diameter of the brush in pixels. One pixel is 4 m.
The value to paint: a row of {0} with an ID from 0 to 255. Rows are shown in their srcR/G/B colour, which the game doesn't read.
{0} isn't loaded, or has no rows from 0 to 255.

Fade every value except the selected one, to see where it is painted. With None selected, None is drawn white.
Outline each map information tile. Tiles with unsaved changes are outlined in amber.
